deckTitle: The Optical Octagon: Focal Points & Retinal Rebels

cards.power: The Clear Breach. If Corny is scratched, the Light Punks scatter into painful chaos.
cards.lore: The strongest refractor. Corny breathes O2 directly from the air. Inflammation (Keratitis) creates permanent vandalism (scars) on the lens.
cards.gradeReason: Armadillo metaphor lands; 'Light Punks' is fun but needs context to fully perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Gritty watercolor. Subject: Armadillo with sparking fly-aura. Mood: Bristling, transparent, besieged.

cards.power: The Inflation Pump. Fills the chamber to keep the eye from collapsing.
cards.lore: Drained via the Canal of Schlemm. If the drain is sabotaged, Aquas builds up until the pressure turns lethal for the nerves.
cards.gradeReason: Pufferfish pressure-gauge image is unforgettable; player knows exactly what to embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor. Subject: Pufferfish attached to pressure gauge in eye chamber. Mood: Tense, inflated, dangerous.

cards.power: The Light Gate. Regulates the photon-count entering the ring.
cards.lore: Controlled by Autonomic Tug-of-War. Sympathetics pull her wide (Fear); Parasympathetics shut her tight (Rest).
cards.gradeReason: Owl gatekeeper is immediately performable; Mydriasis/Miosis tension is built into the role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Industrial watercolor. Subject: Owl in hard hat controlling giant aperture vault door. Mood: Vigilant, authoritative.

cards.power: The Lens Squeezer. Sid pulls the strings to make the lens round for near-vision.
cards.lore: When Sid relaxes, the lens flattens for distance. As we age, the lens gets too stiff for Sid to squeeze (Presbyopia).
cards.gradeReason: Octopus pulling strings on a lens is pure visual kinetics — play Sid, pull strings, done.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor. Subject: Octopus gripping rope-array around transparent lens disc. Mood: Straining, precise, aging.

cards.power: The Fine-Tuner. Provides the final adjustment for a sharp image on the sensor.
cards.lore: Crystal stays clear until proteins denature. She is the only part of the camera that can change shape.
cards.gradeReason: Beaver polishing a lens is charming; 'Fine-Tuner' is solid but not viscerally playable alone.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Workshop watercolor. Subject: Beaver carefully buffing a clear lens disc. Mood: Meticulous, luminous, fragile.

cards.power: The Fog Machine. Dims the world and creates a Halo glare.
cards.lore: Carl is the physical manifestation of oxidized lens proteins. He effectively pulls a dirty curtain over the camera.
cards.gradeReason: Moth drawing dusty curtain over camera lens — you immediately know what Carl does at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dusty watercolor. Subject: Moth dragging yellowed curtain across camera lens. Mood: Dim, hazy, insidious.

cards.power: The Phaco-Blast. Phil pulverizes Cataract Carl in seconds and vacuums up the debris.
cards.lore: The modern surgical exorcism of the lens. Phil clears the stage for the artificial replacement.
cards.gradeReason: Woodpecker with ultrasound drill shredding ice block — action is immediate, violent, satisfying.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kinetic watercolor. Subject: Red-crested woodpecker firing drill-gun at shattering cloudy cube. Mood: Explosive, precise.

cards.power: The Permanent View. A plastic lens that restores clarity forever.
cards.lore: Irene cannot accommodate like Crystal did, so the patient usually trades near-vision for distance clarity.
cards.gradeReason: Robot turtle installing glowing lens is striking; trade-off lore makes Irene interesting but slightly expository.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Sci-fi watercolor. Subject: Robot-turtle carefully inserting glowing disc into giant eyeball. Mood: Precise, permanent, clinical.

cards.power: The Distance Blur. Sees the ant on his knee, but the bus is a ghost.
cards.lore: The eye is too long for the lens's power. Correct with Minus (Concave) glasses to push the light back.
cards.gradeReason: 'Sees the ant on his knee, but the bus is a ghost' — this line alone is a G1 knockout.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor sketch. Subject: Kangaroo squinting at distant bus while noticing ant on knee. Mood: Close-focused, blurry-distant.

cards.power: The Near-Focus Strain. Paul has to work hard even to see the horizon.
cards.lore: The eye is too short. The light aims behind the Retina. Correct with Plus (Convex) glasses to pull the light forward.
cards.gradeReason: Gazelle straining to see the horizon is a good metaphor; less punchy than Minus-Max's ant/bus line.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor. Subject: Gazelle running at wall while squinting at horizon. Mood: Strained, effortful, short-sighted.

cards.power: The Fun-House Mirror. Everything is distorted because the focus is uneven.
cards.lore: Corny Cornea is shaped like a rugby ball instead of a basketball. Light has two different focal lines.
cards.gradeReason: 'Rugby ball instead of basketball' is textbook-clear; Fun-House Mirror tells you instantly how to play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Distorted watercolor. Subject: Rhino with spiral-eyes seeing warped double reflections. Mood: Warped, confused, asymmetric.

cards.power: The Arm-Extender. Pete has to hold the newspaper in the next room to read it.
cards.lore: Not a refractive error, but a mechanical failure. Crystal the Lens has simply become too stiff for Ciliary Sid to squeeze.
cards.gradeReason: 'Newspaper in the next room' is perfect comedy; sloth with reading glasses commits to the bit fully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor. Subject: Sloth in thick glasses holding newspaper at arm's full extension. Mood: Resigned, aging, stiff.

cards.power: The Peripheral Fade. Gus steals the edges of the world until only a tunnel is left.
cards.lore: High IOP kills the axons at the optic disc. It is painless and permanent.
cards.gradeReason: 'Steals the edges of the world until only a tunnel is left' — haunting, exact, immediately embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dark atmospheric watercolor. Subject: Werewolf carrying picture frame with stolen peripheral vision. Mood: Stealthy, irreversible, painless.

cards.power: The Red-Eye Rock. Sudden agony, nausea, and Halos around lights.
cards.lore: The door (angle) to the drain slams shut. Aquas is trapped. The optic nerve starts dying instantly.
cards.gradeReason: Hippo flooding a sealed vault — claustrophobic panic is immediately felt; textbook acute angle-closure.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Urgent watercolor. Subject: Hippo trapped in flooding vault with door slammed shut. Mood: Agony, trapped, catastrophic.

cards.power: The Drain Opener. Increases the back-door (uveoscleral) outflow of Aquas.
cards.lore: Pete makes the drain wider. Side effects: Long lashes and turning blue eyes brown.
cards.gradeReason: Otter with giant wrench opening drain pipe is solid; side-effect lore is memorable but role is mostly mechanical.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Plumber watercolor. Subject: Otter in overalls opening massive pipe valve with flood of fluid. Mood: Practical, draining, prostaglandin.

cards.power: The Pump-Stopper. Cuts the production of Aquas at the source.
cards.lore: Less fluid entering means less pressure. Careful: Timmy can sneak into the lungs and cause Bron[chospasm — text cut off at margin].
cards.gradeReason: Bear cranking pipe valve is strong industrial imagery; lung side-effect warning is important but text clipped.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Industrial watercolor. Subject: Bear in leather jacket cranking shut a massive pressure valve. Mood: Forceful, blocking, risky.

cards.power: The Pixel Army. Roddy sees grey shadows; Conny sees neon colors.
cards.lore: Roddy is the night-fighter (Periphery); Conny is the day-sniper (Macula).
cards.gradeReason: Owl army vs. peacock army in a colosseum — the rod/cone duality is unforgettable as a visual.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Epic watercolor. Subject: Colosseum split between grey owl-warriors and neon peacock-soldiers. Mood: Dual, pixel-army, vivid.

cards.power: The Central Hole. You can see the clock, but never the time.
cards.lore: Mac destroys the fovea. In the Wet form, Annie-VEGF floods the sensor with blood.
cards.gradeReason: 'You can see the clock, but never the time' — the single best line in the deck. Absolute G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Noir watercolor. Subject: Raccoon pouring black ink over TV center while clock face stays visible. Mood: Central void, insidious.

cards.power: The Falling Curtain. A dark shadow moves across the field of vision.
cards.lore: Fluid gets behind the Retina and peels it off. Without the blood supply underneath, the Retina dies.
cards.gradeReason: Baboon ripping wallpaper in flood — visceral, spatial, immediately translates to curtain falling across vision.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Horror watercolor. Subject: Baboon tearing retinal wallpaper off eyeball wall with water pouring behind. Mood: Peeling, catastrophic.

cards.power: The Capillary Pop. Sugar-sludge causes micro-aneurysms and leaks.
cards.lore: Chronic ischemia forces Debbie to summon Annie-VEGF, who builds fragile, bleeding [vessels — text cut off at margin].
cards.gradeReason: Sugar glider smashing pipes is vivid; lore text clipped at margin and two-step mechanism requires explanation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Red-tinged watercolor. Subject: Sugar glider with hammer smashing leaking capillary pipes. Mood: Leaking, fragile, chronic.

cards.lore: If Otto is inflamed (Optic Neuritis), vision fades and eyes hurt when they move. The classic MS sign.
cards.gradeReason: Rat chewing fiber-optic cable is perfect for CN II; MS sign in lore is high-yield but power is terse.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dark watercolor. Subject: Rat severing glowing fiber-optic cable bundle in tunnel. Mood: Cut connection, sparking, painful.

cards.lore: Pam isn't an eye disease; she's a brain alarm. High intracranial pressure pushes the nerves into the eye.
cards.gradeReason: 'Pam isn't an eye disease; she's a brain alarm' — the reframe alone earns G1. Players recalibrate instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Alarm watercolor. Subject: Fly trapped in red-alert siren dome against swollen optic nerve background. Mood: Urgent, systemic warning.

cards.lore: As Vinnie shrinks with age, he pulls away from the wall. His shadows are the flies you see in the sky.
cards.gradeReason: 'His shadows are the flies you see in the sky' — everyone has seen floaters; this card is immediately personal.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Cosmic watercolor. Subject: Translucent jellyfish drifting through dark starry vitreous. Mood: Gelatinous, aging, floaty.

cards.lore: Annie builds vessels where they don't belong. They leak, they bleed, and they cause sca[rs — text cut off at margin].
cards.gradeReason: Ant on bulldozer plowing through flower garden is excellent; 'Illegal Road Builder' is strong but lore clips.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Chaotic watercolor. Subject: Armored ant driving bulldozer through fragile pink garden vessels. Mood: Reckless, leaking, overgrown.

cards.lore: Inflammation of the outer skin. Bacterial Pete brings the pus; Viral Pete brings the water.
cards.gradeReason: Pig with goo-buckets is visceral; Bacterial/Viral split in lore is clinically useful but requires explanation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Green-yellow watercolor. Subject: Weeping pink pig carrying two buckets of pus and water. Mood: Infected, itchy, red.

cards.lore: Karl is deep and dangerous. He leaves scars on Corny that light can't pass through.
cards.gradeReason: Ferret clawing a glass disc is strong; 'Cornea-Ripper' is effective but slightly plain as a standalone power.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Aggressive watercolor. Subject: Ferret slashing claws through cracking glass cornea disc. Mood: Deep, scarring, dangerous.

cards.lore: The immune system attacks the iris. Ursula loves to hang out with Rheuma-Rick.
cards.gradeReason: 'Loves to hang out with Rheuma-Rick' is a smart cross-card connection; role needs more vivid embodiment cue.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Warm inflammatory watercolor. Subject: Hedgehog shooting quills at owl-gatekeeper iris from inside. Mood: Internal, immune-fueled, ciliary flush.

cards.lore: Infection inside the eyeball. Ed can turn the eye into a bag of pus in 24 hours.
cards.gradeReason: 'Turn the eye into a bag of pus in 24 hours' — visceral, urgent, zero ambiguity. Ed knows what he is.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Toxic watercolor. Subject: Glowing radioactive green frog with biohazard symbol oozing inside eyeball. Mood: Nuclear, post-op panic.

cards.lore: Chronic inflammation of the lid. Bill clogs the oil pipes, making the tears evaporate too fast.
cards.gradeReason: Walrus scraping clogged pipes is fitting; 'Crusty Margin' lands as a name but role is descriptive-first.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Grimy watercolor. Subject: Walrus scraping yellow crust off plumbing pipes at eyelid margin. Mood: Chronic, clogged, dry.

cards.lore: An acute pustule at the lid edge. Stan is a localized riot in a gland.
cards.gradeReason: 'Localized riot in a gland' is sharp phrasing; angry boar with biohazard shield makes Stan immediately playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Inflammatory watercolor. Subject: Angry boar with spiked club and biohazard shield erupting at lid margin. Mood: Acute, painful, pustular.

cards.lore: A painless, hard nodule. Chester is the aftermath of a blocked oil gland that didn't clear.
cards.gradeReason: Giant-boulder tortoise is a solid granuloma metaphor; Chester is more descriptive than performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor. Subject: Tortoise carrying enormous smooth grey boulder on shell. Mood: Painless, hard, chronic granuloma.

cards.lore: The lid turns in, and the lashes act like sandpaper on Corny Cornea.
cards.gradeReason: 'Lashes act like sandpaper on Corny Cornea' is sensory perfection — Enno the echidna is already performing it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Abrasive watercolor. Subject: Echidna curling inward with spines scratching against glass wall. Mood: Inward-turning, scratching, painful.

cards.lore: The eyes aren't looking at the same spot. This creates two different stories for the brain.
cards.gradeReason: Chameleon with wall-eyes reading two books is delightful; 'two different stories for the brain' is a good lore hook.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Pastel watercolor. Subject: Chameleon with divergent eyes reading two different books simultaneously. Mood: Misaligned, double-vision, pediatric.

cards.lore: If Stevie isn't fixed, the brain simply deletes the image from the weaker eye. Annie stays lazy forever.
cards.gradeReason: 'The brain simply deletes the image from the weaker eye' — deletion metaphor is clinically precise and chilling.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Lazy watercolor. Subject: Sloth director in chair ignoring camera pointed at black screen. Mood: Suppressed, permanent, neural.

cards.lore: The most dangerous sign in a child. Could be a Cataract or a Retinoblastoma monster.
cards.gradeReason: 'The most dangerous sign in a child' — alarm is immediate; snow leopard with white eye-beam is unforgettable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Eerie watercolor. Subject: Snow leopard with glowing white pupil casting white beam in dark room. Mood: Alarming, pediatric emergency.

cards.lore: The drain to the nose is blocked. Olli makes the baby weep 24/7.
cards.gradeReason: Corked crocodile overflowing with tears is vivid; 'baby weep 24/7' is specific and memorable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor. Subject: Crocodile with cork stuck in snout weeping endless streams. Mood: Blocked, overflowing, infant.

cards.lore: The Fight wire is cut. The pupil stays small, the lid drops, and the face stays dry.
cards.gradeReason: Basset hound cutting wires with pliers is solid; Miosis/Ptosis/Anhydrosis triad is accurate but needs enumeration.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Electrical watercolor. Subject: Droopy hound cutting fight-wire with sparks flying. Mood: Cut connection, asymmetric face, ptosis.

cards.lore: Reacts to near objects but ignores light. The classic red flag for Neurosyphilis.
cards.gradeReason: 'The Prostitute's Pupil' — scandalous, medically precise mnemonic. No one forgets this card ever.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Night-scene watercolor. Subject: Fox with pocket watch ignoring spotlight, focused on held object. Mood: Dissociated, clinical infamy.

cards.lore: A large pupil that reacts very sluggishly to light. Usually a post-viral glitch in the ciliary ganglion.
cards.gradeReason: Snail with flashlight is fitting; 'sluggishly to light' is a natural extension of the metaphor — decent but not thrilling.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Slow watercolor. Subject: Snail with tiny flashlight barely reacting to ambient light. Mood: Sluggish, parasympathetic, post-viral.

cards.lore: A pituitary tumor presses on Charlie. You lose your wingman vision on both sides.
cards.gradeReason: 'You lose your wingman vision on both sides' — pilot metaphor for bitemporal hemianopsia is vivid and table-ready.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Blueprint watercolor. Subject: Pigeon with aviation goggles pecking pituitary anvil on traffic pole. Mood: Crossing, bitemporal loss.

cards.lore: A specific patch of the sensor is dead.
cards.gradeReason: Power and lore are flat for such a quirky-named card; mole-in-perimetry-chart image needed stronger text.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Technical watercolor. Subject: Mole emerging from black void in perimetry target chart. Mood: Dead patch, focal, diagnostic.

cards.lore: You lose the entire left or right side of the world.
cards.gradeReason: Bat with half-black visual field is effective; lore is accurate but very bare — one strong image short of G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Split-field watercolor. Subject: Bat in moonlight with entire right world black, left world lit. Mood: Half-world, stroke, cortex.

cards.lore: Quentin only steals a slice of the pie (e.g., Pie in the Sky deficit).
cards.gradeReason: 'Pie in the Sky deficit' is a genuine mnemonic gem hiding in lore; the card rewards closer reading.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Aerial watercolor. Subject: Magpie stealing one quarter wedge from pie chart floating in sky. Mood: Partial, Meyer's loop, cerebral.

cards.lore: Izzy draws the map of where the sensors are working and where they are dark.
cards.gradeReason: Spider-web perimetry image is beautiful but 'The Cartographer' is purely descriptive — no invitation to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Mapping watercolor. Subject: Spider weaving symmetrical web with light and dark zones marked. Mood: Systematic, diagnostic, perimetric.

cards.lore: Alice blocks the Constrict signal. You stay dilated for days and can't read.
cards.gradeReason: 'You stay dilated for days and can't read' — consequence is immediate and experiential; lemur commits fully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Apothecary watercolor. Subject: Wide-eyed lemur reading book with saucer-pupils, candles blurring. Mood: Dilated, blinded, antimuscarinic.

cards.lore: Phil forces the pupil to shrink, which pulls the trabecular meshwork open to drain Aquas.
cards.gradeReason: Weasel lassoing eyeball to drain bowl is clever; mechanism requires following the chain — solid G2.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor. Subject: Weasel with lasso pulling giant eyeball toward drain bowl. Mood: Constricting, draining, glaucoma-counter.

cards.lore: Stops the immune riot in Uveitis. Warning: Long-term Dot invites Cataract-Carl.
cards.gradeReason: 'Long-term Dot invites Cataract-Carl' is a great cross-card callback; shield metaphor works but isn't electrifying.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Apothecary watercolor. Subject: Polar bear holding ice shield blocking flaming arrows. Mood: Cooling, sterile, double-edged.

cards.lore: Flo stains the gaps in Corny Cornea. Under blue light, she reveals every ulcer and scratch.
cards.gradeReason: Bloodhound detective with orange dye and blue light — every detail slots into the role; Flo is immediately playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Neon-blue watercolor. Subject: Hound detective in trench coat dripping orange dye, scanning window under blue flashlight. Mood: Revealing, forensic.

cards.lore: Larry planes the surface of the eye to fix the focus.
cards.gradeReason: Mantis with excimer blade carving cornea block is visually sharp; lore is terse but accurate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Surgical watercolor. Subject: Mantis with laser-scalpel precisely carving flat cube of cornea. Mood: Precise, refractive, surgical.

cards.lore: Vin removes Vinnie-the-Jelly to clear out blood or reach Detach-Dan.
cards.gradeReason: 'The Jelly-Vac' is punchy and mechanical; cross-card references to Vinnie and Dan are great continuity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Surgical watercolor. Subject: Elephant surgeon in scrubs vacuuming red jelly from massive mixing bowl. Mood: Posterior segment, extraction.

cards.lore: A silicone band squeezed around the eye to push the wall back against the peeling Retina.
cards.gradeReason: Snake squeezing beach-ball eye is a perfect scleral buckle image; power is terse but accurate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Constricting watercolor. Subject: Python coiling tight silicone band around inflated beach-ball eyeball. Mood: Squeezing, scleral, mechanical.

cards.lore: Ted burns small holes in the meshwork to help Aquas escape Gus-the-Glaucoma.
cards.gradeReason: Dragon scorching drain grate with green laser is vivid; naming Gus-the-Glaucoma ties the arc together.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Steam-punk watercolor. Subject: Mechanical dragon firing argon laser at drain grating with escaping fluid. Mood: Burning, meshwork, glaucoma-fix.

cards.lore: The Attending's favorite tool to find the Flare in the soup.
cards.gradeReason: 'Find the Flare in the soup' is a memorable attending-culture line; giraffe at biomicroscope is charming.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Clinical watercolor. Subject: Giraffe in lab coat bending over steampunk slit-lamp microscope. Mood: Elevated, clinical, inspection.

cards.lore: Looking at the only place in the body where you can see live nerves and vessels.
cards.gradeReason: Anglerfish diving into retinal tunnel is a strong image; lore fact is gold-standard but power is brief.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Deep-sea watercolor. Subject: Anglerfish with bioluminescent lure entering glowing retinal tunnel. Mood: Deep, intimate, vascular.

cards.lore: Localize the glitch. Is it the pump, the window, or the cable?
cards.gradeReason: 'The Pimp-Master' is medical school gold; 'Is it the pump, the window, or the cable?' is the perfect diagnostic frame.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Boss-level watercolor. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit on throne of ophthalmology textbooks, pointing accusingly. Mood: Attending, omniscient, pimp.

verdict: The Optical Octagon is arguably the tightest MedKayfab deck in the corpus — 55 cards covering anatomy, pathology, pharmacology, surgery, and neuro-ophthalmology with almost no dead weight. Mac-the-Degenerate's 'clock you can never read' line and Glauco-Gus's 'tunnel vision' metaphor are among the best power/lore pairings in the entire series. The two G3 cards (Scotoma Scott, Isopter Izzy) have strong visuals but flat text — names carry more than the copy. Three lore texts clipped at page margin. Table-ready: Yes.
blurb: 55 unforgettable characters from cornea to cortex, turning ophthalmology's scariest conditions into creatures you can name, describe, and defeat. Perfect for medical students who actually want to remember what they learned.

coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — 'The Optical Octagon: Focal Points & Retinal Rebels' is genuinely clever and memorable

notes: 55 cards (not 56) — page 15 bottom-right quadrant is a non-card 'Optical Octagon Quests' scroll with 4 gameplay quests (Angle-Al, Detach-Dan, Glauco-Gus, Mac-the-Degenerate). Three lore texts clipped at right margin: Timmy-the-Block (Bron[chospasm]), Diabetic Debbie (bleeding [vessels]), Annie-VEGF (sca[rs]). Typo on Buckle Bob stat: 'Scleral Encirclment' should be 'Encirclement'. Pages have distinct border-design themes by section: IOP pressure gauges (p5), spiderwebs (p6), brains+aliens (p7), green germ-blobs (p8), mice-with-rakes (p9), toys+aliens (p10), electrical circuits (p11), navigation tools+aliens (p12), apothecary bottles (p13), gears+tools (p14), mixed spectacle (p15). Excellent cross-card referencing throughout (Carl invites Dot; Gus defeated by Pete/Timmy/Ted; Dan fixed by Vin/Bob; Annie-VEGF summoned by Debbie/Mac; Ursula hangs out with Rheuma-Rick).

urgent: Fix 3 clipped lore texts at right margin (Timmy-the-Block, Diabetic Debbie, Annie-VEGF)
Fix typo: 'Encirclment' should be 'Encirclement' on Buckle Bob
quickWins: Give Scotoma Scott a punchier power line — 'A specific patch of the sensor is dead' undersells the name
Give Isopter Izzy a performative hook beyond cartography metaphor

Consider adding RAF dice to anatomy cards (Corny, Crystal, Iris) for mechanical play

marketingText:
MedKayfab: OPHTHALMOLOGY – The Optical Octagon (Medical Mnemonics Cut & Play Comic)

55 illustrated medical mnemonic cards to master the painless thieves of vision, the red eye that actually means trouble, and the retina that reads like a systemic diary.

A patient sits down and tells you the bottom half of the world went grey this morning, like a curtain rising from the floor. No pain. No redness. Nothing for the penlight to catch. You have minutes to decide whether this is a retina peeling off its wall, a vessel that clotted in the night, or a nerve going dark behind a quiet eye, because two of those answers come with a clock and one of them does not care how calm the front of the eye looks. Ophthalmology is the specialty where the worst emergencies arrive without a single sign you can see from across the room.

MedKayfab Ophthalmology turns the eye from cornea to cortex into a narrative wrestling match, where every condition that can dim a field shows up as a character you can name on sight. Stop drilling the fundus atlas as a wall of look-alike photographs. Start performing the diagnosis.

YOU'LL GET
- 55 illustrated MedKayfab cards (4 cards per page)
- Full MedKayfab Freestyle rules (Quest Die mechanics)
- The Optical Octagon Quests scroll, four chained scenarios that make you cross-examine Angle-Al, Detach-Dan, Glauco-Gus, and Mac-the-Degenerate as a single case instead of four flashcards
- S-Tier characters like Mac-the-Degenerate, Glauco-Gus, and Argyll Robertson Al
- Free lifetime updates as guidelines evolve
- CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence, print, share, and adapt freely
- PDF optimized for home printing (A4 / Letter)

What's in the deck
The deck is built around the eye's quietest predators. Mac-the-Degenerate, the Center Thief, robs the middle out of every face the patient loves and leaves the edges untouched, so they still walk in unaided but cannot read a word off the chart. Glauco-Gus, the Silent Thief, raises the pressure so slowly and so painlessly that he has already pocketed the outer field before anyone notices the tunnel closing in. Argyll Robertson Al is the pupil that accommodates but refuses to react to light, a small neurological tell that points straight back to old syphilis and reminds you the eye is never just the eye. Around them sit the retinal vessels that bleed on a diabetic's schedule, the angle that slams shut into a rock-hard red eye, and the drops that quietly trigger a wheeze two organs away.

How it works
Every card is a cognitive anchor: the Character (the mnemonic), the Visual (the scene), the Stat Block (pressures, fields, defining signs), the Lore (the clinical story), and the Quest (the challenge that makes you commit). The Mechanism Flash mode is the test that matters: name the lesion and the field defect it carries in one sentence without looking, or the vision you were asked to save is already gone. Because the characters cross-reference each other, beating Glauco-Gus pulls in the drugs that drop his pressure, and summoning the bleeding retina drags in the diabetes that fed it.

Honest cognitive load
This is a dense, sign-heavy deck built for medical students on their ophthalmology rotation, optometry students, and anyone who keeps confusing one painless field loss for another the night before an exam. The reasoning is concrete rather than algorithm-heavy, so it rewards repeat passes more than raw effort. It pairs naturally with Neuroanatomy for the back half of the visual pathway once the signal leaves the retina, and with an internal medicine or endocrinology deck for the diabetic and hypertensive eyes that turn the fundus into a window on the whole body.

ABOUT MEDKAYFAB
MedKayfab is a narrative medical learning card game, 50 decks covering the full medical curriculum. Every card encodes a clinical mechanism as a character with a personality, a story, and a reasoning challenge. Built by a physician. Assembled with AI tools. Manually revised. Honest about its limitations. Free to use, share, and adapt under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

PAY WHAT YOU WANT
This deck is Pay What You Want, including free. If you find it useful, a fair price is €5. Student on a budget? Enter €0, no questions asked. Want to support more decks? Anything above fair price is appreciated. Share freely, attribute honestly, never resell.

DISCLAIMER
MedKayfab is a learning companion, not a clinical reference. Content was created by a physician and reviewed to the best of our knowledge, but medicine evolves, guidelines change, and some mechanisms in here will be simplified or wrong. Always verify against current primary sources and clinical guidelines before applying anything to patient care. The Blödsinn! is the vehicle. The science is serious.

Stay fluffy. — Doc FrizzleBob
